newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends down on profit taking, market firm.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends down on profit taking, market firm.

text.p: IPE Brent crude closed down on Thursday amid late profit taking with all eyes fixed on NYMEX heating oil, the current driving force of the energy complex.
November Brent last traded 27 cents down at $22.93 a barrel having touched $23.40 during the session. Dealers said the fundamentals indicated continued firmness, despite the dip lower.
Most support for Brent was derived from NYMEX heating oil where October contracts broke through 72.25 cents a gallon, its highest level in five years, and toyed briefly with 72.80 cents.
Heating oil was also the hostage of profit taking before the close and prices were pushed 77 cents to 71.00 cents a gallon.
Despite the fall, dealers saw continued firmness in the heating oil market since most volume was conducted at the higher levels.
"We had 70 percent of volume between 71.25 and 72.30 and although we broke 72.25 we need to see more volume above this level," said one trader who added, "There's still respect for 72.25."
The price of heating oil has risen by more than 25 percent over the last three months on supply tightness in the U.S. and Europe.
Gas oil closed $6.75 a tonne higher at $231.75 having gained ground on the back of tight physical supplies coupled with good demand and stronger NYMEX heating oil.
"Gas oil led the way earlier in the day and then passed on the baton to heating oil," commented one dealer.
